ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with a side length of 4. Point $P$ is on $AB$. Through point $P$, draw $PE\perp AC$ with the foot of the perpendicular as $E$. Extend $BC$ to point $Q$ such that $CQ=PA$. Connect $PQ$ and let it intersect $AC$ at point $D$. Find the length of $DE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $PF \parallel BC$ through point P intersecting $AC$ at F, then $\angle FPD = \angle Q$, $\angle APF = \angle B$, $\angle AFP = \angle ACB$,

$\because$ $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,

$\therefore$ $\angle B = \angle A = \angle ACB = 60^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\angle APF = \angle AFP = \angle A = 60^\circ$,

$\therefore$ $\triangle APF$ is an equilateral triangle, and $PE \perp AC$,

$\therefore$ AP=PF, AE=EF, and AP=CQ,

$\therefore$ PF=CQ,

In $\triangle PDF$ and $\triangle QDC$,

$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle FPD = \angle Q \\
\angle PDF = \angle QDC \\
PF = CQ
\end{array}\right.$,

$\therefore$ $\triangle PDF \cong \triangle QDC$ (AAS),

$\therefore$ FD=CD,

$\therefore$ EF + FD = AE + CD,

$\therefore$ DE = $\frac{1}{2}$AC, and AC=4,

$\therefore$ DE = \boxed{2}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle, A is above, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right. Point P is located on side AB. Through P, draw a perpendicular to side AC, with foot E, so A, E, D, and C are on the same side AC. Side BC is extended to the right of C to Q, and segment PQ intersects AC at D. Reasoning: Establish a coordinate system according to the specified method, let AC be the x-axis, and take A=(0,0), C=(4,0). Because ABC is an equilateral triangle with side length 4, B=(2,-2√3) can be taken. Let AP=t, then P moves t units from A along the direction of AB, so P=(t/2,-√3t/2). Since PE is perpendicular to AC, E is the projection of P on the x-axis, therefore E=(t/2,0). Also because CQ=PA=t, and Q is on the extension of BC past C; the unit direction vector from B to C is (1/2,√3/2), so Q=C+t(1/2,√3/2)=(4+t/2,√3t/2). Segment PQ intersects AC, that is y=0, at D. The y-coordinate of P is -√3t/2, and the y-coordinate of Q is √3t/2; the two are symmetric about the x-axis, so the intersection point D of PQ and y=0 is exactly the midpoint of PQ. Thus the x-coordinate of D is [(t/2)+(4+t/2)]/2=2+t/2, that is D=(2+t/2,0). Therefore DE=(2+t/2)-t/2=2.
